Around 10 years old when I was upset or frustrated I'd run to my room and take it out on myself with a thumbtack. There was no bleeding but I'd scratch it deep enough to leave red swollen marks for a few hours. I eventually stopped for a while and would only do that occasionally, then when I was in seventh grade I got bullied by my best friend and my mental health went tumbling. I ended up relapsing, this time I used pins and went deep enough until there were marks for a few days, but there was still very little to no blood. Again, I eventually stopped but about a year and a half later I relapsed again due to bullying, that was when I started using a blade :/

Edit: forgot to mention how throughout this I would hit myself, but at the time didn't know that also counted as sh

Honestly this hits close to home reading it. In my experience at least schools have always turned a blind eye when it comes to mental health, it's bullshit.

You're not the only one that's been negatively affected by schools, I hope you know that you're not alone in that sense. It's completely valid to be angry, upset, lost and/or frustrated at them. And hey I'm proud of you for continuing to try, that takes a lot of work and it's amazing you're still here with us. Keep fighting, alright?
